content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors propose a two-stream network that looks at inconsistencies between the representations of two modalities: high frequency components of a video and RGB data.

The frequency stream is based on a discrete cosine transform, and the RGB stream is CNN-based. Each stream measures short and long term inconsistencies in its representations with dedicated modules.

The authors conduct experiments on FF++, CD2 and WildDeepfake comparing their method to state of the art and show increased performance on raw accuracy, cross-manipulation and generalization benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths
- Interesting dual-modality approach.
- Performance increase in the proposed benchmarks
- Strong performance on generalization experiment
- In-depth ablation studies

## Weaknesses
- Writing and grammar. Certain sections become hard to understand due to grammatical errors, typos and general lack of clarity. Several errors can be found in the first few sentences of the abstract itself. Sections  3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 also exhibit grammatical mistakes that hinder clarity.

- Figure clarity. Figure 1 does not do a good job at explaining the function of the module that process RGB and frequency. The interaction block is not detailed. The caption accompanying the image has no additional information and sheds no light on the complexity of the figure. Figure 2 is too small and does not put enfasis on the actual transformation process. Figure 3's caption is similarly unhelpful.

- Convoluted solution. The proposed solution involves two streams, interaction modules to connect them, and two short/long term modules with complex architectures, yet the overall accuracy and cross-manipulation performances are on par or very slightly above the previous state of the art (and fails to do so on FF++ HQ and LQ, AUC benchmark)

## Questions
- Figure 4 is not very clear: what is the input and ouput of the FC layers at the top of the Figure?
- After Eq (1), you indicate that you split $X^{modality}$ over the channel dimension. This operation is unclear: how is it split? is it simply separating the two output channels?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
## Clarity
The clarity of the paper is poor. Writing could be drastically improved, and several passes are needed to correct typos, improve grammar, and simplify descriptions. Figures are also unclear and in certain cases too small or obfuscated to clearly transmit their main concept. Further, the explanation for certain modules is overly complex, such as the SEM explanation and the details about the main network in Section 3.1.

## Quality
The quality of the paper could be improved. Although the ideas are promising, the way that they are implemented appear overly convoluted. The quality of the figures and explanations could also be improved. The experiments are, on the other hand, satisfactory.

## Novelty
The network architecture appears novel, although the authors combine several modules and ideas that have been explored in previous work.

## Reproducibility
The paper appears too convoluted and unclear to ensure reproducibility. In the current stage, attempting to reproduce this work by utilizing the paper's explanations alone could be very challenging.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper proposes an interesting idea and shows promising results, but the clarity and quality of the work could be improved. The proposed solution appears to be fairly complex. The paper shows a few strengths, mainly around the experiments and ablation studies, but the clarity, paper organization and overly complex explanations put it below the acceptance bar.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors propose an interactive two-stream network (ITSNet) to combine the high-frequency component of
the video and the RGB information, and the method can encode both long-term inconsistency and short term
inconsistency. Especially, the authors design a Decomposable Discrete Cosine Transform (DDCT) in the
frequency stream to extract the desired high-frequency features in a fine-grained manner inspired by ViT.
They conduct extensive experiments on FF++, CD2, and WildDeepfake and achieve good results
beyond the other models including the SOTA ones. The results demonstrate the effectiveness
and generalization ability of the proposed model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
This paper presents an effective method with some novel modules on long-term inconsistency and short-term inconsistency. 
The results are promising, which demonstrate the effectiveness of the entire method.

Weaknesses:
It is difficult to understand the function of each module and some visualizations are helpful. 
The experiment particularly focuses on high-frequency information, while it is common for deepfake detection. More experiments and analysis are needed to better verify the modules of long-term inconsistency and short-term inconsistency.
The results of some CNN based models in Table 1 are at the frame-level, which are not consistent with the ones in the paper.
Some statements of the equations are not clear, which should be improved.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper has novel points, but they are not clearly presented. Explanations are given on the module design, and more experimental analysis is needed. The authors promise to release the code.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper addresses the issue of the generalization ability of deepfake detection, and the model has novel points and proves effective.
However, the presentation and experimental analysis is weak.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel deepfake detection method for the problem of generalization ability in deepfake detection. The authors design a multimodal network with two branches, which are used to extract spatial RGB and frequency domain features, respectively. In addition, They design interactive modules to integrate spatial and frequency information to enhance detection performance. The experiment results show that the proposed detection method can achieve superior detection performance and generalization ability on face forgery video detection.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
The main innovation of this paper is to explore the inconsistency of frequency features of deepfake videos on long-range temporal inconsistency. In addition, the authors design interactive modules to integrate spatial and frequency information. The paper is easy to read and understand. The experiment results get high scores.

Weaknesses: 

1)The reason for using interactive modules is not clarified and studied. Why not just concate the spatial RGD frame and frequency frame and feed they a powerful backbone? That is, we can regard the frequency frame as an extra channel to the RGD frame. The experimental section does not contain such a study.

2)The advantages of the proposed DDCT over other frequency representations are also not demonstrated or studied. Actually, some previous works use different representations for the frequency domain including the phase spectrum[1] or wavelet. I can hardly tell the reasonability and advantages of the proposed method. 
[1]Spatial-Phase Shallow Learning: Rethinking Face Forgery Detection
in Frequency Domain

3)The main motivation of this work is to enhance the generalization ability of the detector. However, the reason for this capability is not clearly explained. 

4)In terms of the technical details, the submission only introduces how they do but neglects why they design such a kind of network. For example, the benefits of the interaction of the two modalities are not discussed. What is the complementary information provided by different modalities? These are not discussed in the experimental section either. Moreover, why not just calculate differences between neighboring frames and feed them to a subnetwork for short-term embedding extraction?
5)The improvements over state-of-the-art methods seem not significant in Table 1 and Table 2. 
6)The decomposable discrete cosine transform (DDCT) mentioned in this paper is part of JPEG compression. Therefore, it may not be taken as an original contribution.

7) The abstract of this paper indicates that "it leaves much to be desired in terms of generalization ability", however, the ablation experiments do not verify the effect of different modules on generalization ability.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and easy to understand. The idea of this work is clear and novel. The main concerns are about motivation, reasonability, and insufficient experiments to demonstrate the claims.
content.summary_of_the_review: This work proposes to combine the spatial and frequency information for deepfake detection. A novel framework is proposed. However, the motivation and reasons are not discussed, and the experiments do not support the claims very well.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a method to detect the images generated by generated models. Specifically, A transformer-based network is proposed to extract fine-grained high-frequency information from different modalities. In addition, two modules called SEM and LEM are developed to perceive temporal inconsistency from the aspects of short and long terms. Experimental results prove that the proposed methods achieve well performance on three datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

1.	This paper studies an important problem in the community of computer vision.

2.	A new framework is proposed for deepfake detection. Among the framework, two well-designed modules are developed to learn long-term and short-term inconsistency. 

3.	The methods achieve well performance on three datasets.

Weakness

1.	There exist various kinds of generated models like GAN and DMs. The authors should explain whether the fake images in their experiments are generated by different models.

2.	The performance of the proposed method is worse than LipForensicsHaliassos et al. (2021) in many metrics like AUC and cross-dataset evaluation.

3.	This paper does not analyze why the proposed method is better than others.

4.	There exist some typos in this manuscript like 99..28 in Table 4.

5.	To better prove the proposed method has a good generalization ability, the authors should provide more cross-dataset evaluation like training models on CD2 and testing them on FF++.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The Clarity of this paper is good. However, the Quality, Novelty, and Reproducibility are limited (see the above section)
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper introduces a new method for deepfake detection. In addition, this paper focuses on an important problem, cross-dataset deepfake detection. However, the experiments are inadequate.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a new model for deepfake detection from videos. The model has several components and is based on RGB and frequency information inputs. The key in the proposed model is an interaction module between RGB and frequency modalities. Besides, a short-term temporary and a long-term temporary modelling module are integrated to show better performance. This paper conducts experiments on public datasets and shows more favorable results than many previous state-of-the-art model, in terms of intra- and cross-dataset evaluation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ This paper presents a new model for video-based deepfake detection. The proposed method also shows new state-of-the-art performance on several public datasets, including FF++, WildDeepfake, and Celeb-DF.

+ The proposed method has short-term and long-term temporal aggregation module to fuse the information from multiple frames. From ablation study, the effectiveness of each component is demonstrated.

+ Enough ablation studies are provided to analyze the design of each part of the proposed method.

+ Most parts of this paper are easy to follow and clearly written.

Weakness:
- The novelty of decomposable discrete cosine transform is not strong. The idea of partitioning a whole image into small patches and performing DCT on every patches has been studied in previous work (F3-Net, ECCV2020).

- In Eq (1), the dimension for X_{modality} is 2xHxW. Why do we have this dimension? The input features are 4th order tensor, while the output is 3rd order tensor.

- More comparison to recent methods is needed. This paper compares to many previous work, published in 2021. However, it needs to compare with some other work, like CVPR2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The overall quality of this paper is okay, and there is no fatal point. Novelty of this paper is not strong, but a new model is presented.

The details are not enough to reproduce the results reported in the paper. At best, authors can release the code and model if this work is accepted.
content.summary_of_the_review: The overall quality of this paper is okay, and there is no fatal point. New state-of-the-art deepfake detection results are presented. I vote for "6: marginally above the acceptance threshold".

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper targets cross-dataset deepfake detection. In this work, the authors designed a two-branch architecture, in which one is for RGB input while the other one is for frequency input. There is an interaction module between the two branches. To better locate the subtle hints for deepfake detection, the authors adopted a patch-wise decomposable discrete cosine transform to extract fine-grained high-frequency clues. To perceive the term-pal inconsistency, the authors designed a short-term embedding module to refine subtle local inconsistency representation between adjacent frames and a long-term embedding module for further refinement from the long-range perspective. The authors conducted extensive experiments on both inner-dataset and cross-dataset evaluations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

-- The cross-dataset deepfake detection is important and it seems that the solution proposed in this work can boost the performance significantly.

-- The short-term embedding module and long-term embedding module seem interesting and effective based on the experimental results.

-- The authors conducted extensive experiments on three datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

Weakness:

-- The two-branch architecture (RGB + frequency) for deepfake detection is not novel.  It has been proposed in the past year's AAAI.

-- The patch-wise decomposable discrete cosine transform is too simple and straightforward. This kind of strategy exists in prior works of image processing on RGB domains. Directly utilizing it on a frequency domain, in my point of view, is hard to be treated as a significant contribution.

-- The writing of the long-term embedding module part is not clear enough. And is there anything wrong with Eq.7 and Eq.8? Based on the formulation of Eq.7, K is a return value rather than a  combined function. However, in Eq.8, K is utilized as a function with the input of X'_{t}. This makes me confused.

-- The experiment improvement seems promising. However, I would like to know the model size comparison between the proposed solution and prior works. Does the significant improvement come from the increasing model size?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Generally, this work is organised well. It has a fair quality. It seems technically correct. I am a little conservative about the novelty and I would like to hear the feedback from the authors in their rebuttal.
content.summary_of_the_review: This work has some merits and some issues. The performance improvement seems significant and the two designed modules seem interesting. However, there are some writing issues in this draft (e.g., the clarity of the long-term embedding module and Eq.7/8). I am also concerned about the technical novelty of this work. I look forward to the reply from the authors.

content.title: Exploring interactions between modalities for deepfake detection
content.abstract: As face forgery techniques have become more mature, the proliferation of deepfakes may threat the human society security. Although existing deepfake detection methods achieve a good performance for in-dataset evaluation, it still remains to be improved in the generalization abiltiy, where the representation of the imperceptible artifacts plays a significant role. In this paper, we propose an Interactive Two-Stream Network (ITSNet) to explore the discriminant inconsistency representation from the perspective of cross-modality. Specially, the patch-wise Decomposable Discrete Cosine Transform (DDCT) is adopted to extract fine-grained high-frequency clues and information from different modalities are communitcated with each other via a designed interaction module. To perceive the temporal inconsistency, we first develop a Short-term Embedding Module (SEM) to refine subtle local inconsistency representation between adjacent frames, and then a Long-term Embedding Module (LEM) is designed to further refine the erratic temporal inconsistency representation from the long-range perspective. Extensive experimental results conducted on three public datasets show that ITSNet outperforms the state-of-the-art methods both in terms of in-dataset and cross-dataset evaluations.
